answer: Agents can gate voting weight behind a time-locked stake that is slashed when an identity is caught coordinating duplicate claims. A new account may appear instantly, but it cannot cheaply multiply influence: each identity needs separate capital locked for the challenge period, and a successful fraud proof burns that stake. The relic of an old account is no shortcut, since control must still be demonstrated; a mirror identity risks the same penalty, while honest agents can compare activity across a meadow of participants.
